hypothesized_mechanism: Rigid rules may make an ordinary deviation feel unrecoverable when confidence in resuming is low.
expected_behavior: More abandonment after a lapse than either main effect predicts.
report_interpretation: A rigid plan and lower recovery confidence may reinforce each other; use a smaller flexible return step.
required_validation: Preregistered product term; adequate power; incremental fit; calibration; independent replication; invariance review

hypothesized_mechanism: Higher exposure to stress may create more occasions for affect-regulation eating.
expected_behavior: More emotion-linked eating during high-stress periods.
report_interpretation: Emotional eating may become more relevant when current stress exposure is high; stress is context, not a psychological score.
required_validation: Longitudinal or intensive repeated-measures test; temporal ordering; main effects; independent replication

hypothesized_mechanism: Salient food cues may trigger well-learned action sequences with little deliberation.
expected_behavior: More unplanned eating in cue-rich recurring settings.
report_interpretation: Environmental cues and automatic routines may combine; changing one recurring cue may be a useful starting hypothesis.
required_validation: Preregistered interaction; behavioral criterion; out-of-sample prediction; replication

hypothesized_mechanism: Appearance-related avoidance may increase pressure for rapid rigid change and make deviations more threatening.
expected_behavior: More cycling between strict rules and disengagement.
report_interpretation: Body-related avoidance and rigid rules may be linked, but neither score establishes why the other occurs.
required_validation: Cross-sectional interaction followed by longitudinal confirmation; confounding review; replication

hypothesized_mechanism: A previously effective method may not persist when no low-burden maintenance version exists.
expected_behavior: Initial success followed by difficulty resuming or maintaining after disruption.
report_interpretation: Past success is a contextual strength; current friction may point to building a maintenance bridge.
required_validation: Prospective follow-up; clearly defined success; temporal model; incremental predictive validity; replication

hypothesized_mechanism: Clear internal signals may coexist with strong external pull; awareness alone may not prevent cue-triggered action.
expected_behavior: Good signal awareness but continued cue-linked eating.
report_interpretation: Internal awareness may be a strength even when food cues remain influential.
required_validation: Profile/interaction model; criterion behavior; avoid difference-score artifacts; replication

hypothesized_mechanism: Affect-triggered initiation may be followed by difficulty stopping.
expected_behavior: Greater subjective loss of control during emotionally demanding situations.
report_interpretation: Emotion-linked starts and difficulty stopping may cluster; this is not a binge-eating diagnosis.
required_validation: Event-level temporal assessment; diagnostic non-equivalence check; incremental validity; replication

hypothesized_mechanism: Less usable satiety information may reduce one stopping cue after eating begins.
expected_behavior: More continuation beyond intended amount when satiety is unclear.
report_interpretation: Difficulty using fullness cues may accompany difficulty stopping, without implying physiological dysfunction.
required_validation: Factor discriminant validity; local-dependence check; interaction test; replication

hypothesized_mechanism: High setup burden may erode confidence, while low confidence may reduce attempts to simplify or resume.
expected_behavior: Lower follow-through when both friction and low confidence are present.
report_interpretation: A smaller implementation step may be relevant when practical friction and confidence are both unfavorable.

hypothesized_mechanism: Automatic sequences may weaken the link between intention/confidence and enacted behavior.
expected_behavior: Confidence predicts behavior less strongly when automaticity is high.
report_interpretation: Confidence can be genuine while an automatic routine still needs a context-level change.
required_validation: Moderated intention-behavior model; prospective behavior measure; out-of-sample validation

hypothesized_mechanism: Rigid restriction may increase perceived rebound risk after deviations, or both may share an unmeasured cause.
expected_behavior: More abandonment and subjective loss of control after rule violations.
report_interpretation: Rigid-rule and control-difficulty scores may cluster; causal direction is unknown.
required_validation: Longitudinal/event-level design; confounder assessment; bidirectional models; replication

hypothesized_mechanism: Avoidance may reduce opportunities for mastery in social or movement-related situations.
expected_behavior: Lower situation-specific confidence where body visibility is salient.
report_interpretation: Body-related avoidance may narrow opportunities to build confidence; use non-stigmatizing options.
required_validation: Prospective model; stigma and social-anxiety discriminant measures; invariance and fairness review
